channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy credibility and intervention dynamics – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that the Japanese Yen (JPY) entered the latest Bank of Japan (BoJ) decision and suspected intervention with weak flow momentum and lighter positioning, even as investors remained net long JPY and net short USD/JPY.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD remains under pressure as bond yields, US Dollar rebound
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down 1.7% to near $58.00 during the European trading session on Friday. The white metal continues to decline throughout the day as United States (US) Treasury Yields have bounced back amid fears that inflationary pressures will remain elevated.

item.title: Gold declines as firmer US Dollar, hawkish Fed outlook weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) stabilizes following the previous day’s sharp sell-off, while hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations remain a key headwind for the non-yielding metal.

item.title: Brent: Conflict risks keep prices elevated – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke and colleagues highlight that Brent remains volatile as Middle East tensions and shipping disruptions through key chokepoints constrain supply.

item.title: Japanese Yen dips back to 160.00 against the US Dollar as post-BoJ gains fade
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) posts moderate losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with the USD/JPY pair trading just above 160.00 at the time of writing, after whipsawing within a rough 240-pip range between 158.60 and 161.00 earlier on the day.

item.title: US Dollar Index: DXY seen returning to 96.00–100.00 range – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the Dollar stabilized after a sharp sell-off linked to suspected USD/JPY intervention, but argues the broader USD rally since May has likely ended, with US Dollar Index (DXY) expected to move back into a 96.00–100.00 range.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds firm despite weak Chinese data, fading RBA rate hike bets
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7030 at the time of writing on Friday, little changed on the day after Thursday's strong rally.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Balanced growth supports CAD – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect Canadian real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to rise by 0.2% m/m in May, exceeding the flash estimate and extending April’s 0.5% gain. They highlight balanced growth across goods and services, with manufacturing, existing home sales and retail trade all contributing.

item.title: Indian Rupee sets for bets weekly close in four months
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends the week-long rally against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday.

item.title: Experts agree: The US Dollar rally might have found serious headwinds
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) attempts to cling above the 100.00 psychological level on Friday after a nearly 1.5% selloff in the previous three days, as the Federal Reserve's (Fed) lack of forward guidance at Wednesday's monetary policy meeting raised concerns that the bank might fail on its commitment

item.title: US Dollar: Post-Fed losses extend as positioning unwinds – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar’s post-FOMC selloff has accelerated, with DXY briefly dipping below 100.0 and returning to levels seen after Kevin Warsh’s June press conference. He highlights stretched net-long USD positioning versus G9 and large EUR/USD shorts.

item.title: Euro rebounds vs Yen as BoJ rate hold, Eurozone inflation support
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 184.00 on Friday, stabilizing after the sharp volatility seen on Thursday. The cross plunged to near 182.00 from around 187.00, losing almost 500 pips within minutes after what appears to have been another intervention by Japanese authorities in the foreign exchange market.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Wide range trading outlook – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Alex Loo notes that despite Governor Ueda’s hawkish tone, the Japanese Yen reaction was muted and the BoJ kept its policy rate at 1%.

item.title: Euro hits session lows against the British Pound following Eurozone inflation data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) edges lower against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, hitting session lows at 0.8554 following the Eurozone’s preliminary inflation figures from July.

item.title: British Pound underperforms as traders reconsider BoE interest rate hike bets
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is down against its major currency peers, trading marginally lower at around 1.3444 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.08 per troy ounce, down 1.59% from the $59.02 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: China: Growth drift and export reliance – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists highlight renewed weakness in China, with official PMI data showing both manufacturing and non-manufacturing back in contraction and domestic demand still soft. Policymakers are prioritizing faster implementation of existing measures over new stimulus.

item.title: ECB’s Kocher: Central bank policies will remain data-dependent
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Martin Kocher said in European trade on Friday that recent weeks have demonstrated how quickly geopolitical developments can alter energy prices and, consequently, the inflation outlook.

item.title: British Pound: BoE communication keeps restrictive stance – MUFG
item.description: MUFG analysts use a textual sentiment framework on the latest Bank of England (BoE) decision, finding a hawkish hold in Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) member contributions but a more balanced tone from Governor Bailey’s press conference.

item.title: Eurozone flash headline HICP rises at a stronger pace of 2.9% YoY, as expected
item.description: Annual Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) in the Eurozone, as measured by changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services in the European Monetary Union, rises at a faster pace of 2.9% in July, as expected, against 2.8% in June.

item.title: Gold: Central bank buying offsets ETF outflows – ING
item.description: ING’s commodities team reports that Gold demand was steady in 2Q 2026, with total demand flat year-on-year at 1,269 tonnes as strong central bank purchases balanced weaker ETF demand.

item.title: British Pound: Limited support from BoE policy – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister notes that the Bank of England kept rates unchanged and avoided signalling future hikes, despite a closer-than-expected 6–3 vote and Governor Bailey’s insistence that the BoE is not edging toward tightening.

item.title: WTI Oil drifts closer to $80.00 amid a mild increase in traffic through Hormuz
item.description: Oil prices are ticking lower for the second consecutive day on Friday, with the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel hitting session lows a few cents above $80.00.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Prolonged pause with hike risks – UOB
item.description: UOB strategists observe that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept the Fed Funds Target Rate at 3.50%–3.75% for a fifth meeting, with a 9–3 split as three presidents sought a 25 bps hike.

item.title: Gold weakens towards $4,050 as USD preserves gains on Iran risks and Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its steady intraday descent through the first half of the European session on Friday and hits a fresh daily low, around the $4,060 area in the last hour.

item.title: British Pound struggles to extend recovery against Japanese Yen
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) faces roadblocks in extending the early recovery against the Japanese Yen (JPY) above 216.33 during the European trading session on Friday.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Steadies above June low as bears await 1.4000 breakdown
item.description: The USD/CAD pair seesaws between tepid gains/minor losses through the early European session on Friday, consolidating its recent losses to the lowest level since June 17, touched the previous day.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike path shaped by Iran war – Nomura
item.description: Nomura strategists highlight that Euro area Gross Domestic Product (GDP) excluding Ireland has been growing around potential despite the Iran war.

item.title: Forex Today: Japanese Yen retreats after rallying on suspected intervention, BoJ holds steady
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Friday, July 31:

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks and BoJ stance – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny and Abdul-Ahad Lockhart note that the Japanese Yen surged as USD/JPY dropped from 163.00 to 158.00, in a move they attribute to probable Ministry of Finance intervention during New York trading.
